obligation: NRC cyber notification: attack that adversely impacted safety, security, or EP functions
trigger: Discovery of a cyberattack that adversely impacted safety-related or important-to-safety, security, or emergency preparedness functions (including offsite communications), or that compromised support systems and equipment resulting in such adverse impacts, within the scope of 73.54
deadline: Within 1 hour after discovery
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via the Emergency Notification System (ENS); commercial telephone if ENS is unavailable (73.77(c)(1))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - power reactor licensee under 73.54 (each station decides for itself)
clock_starts: Discovery of the cyberattack at the station
owner: Station shift manager (decision), advised by the Site Cyber Security Program Manager

obligation: NRC cyber notification: attack that could have caused an adverse impact
trigger: Discovery of a cyberattack that could have caused an adverse impact to safety, security, or EP functions, or could have compromised support systems and equipment within the scope of 73.54 (for example, malware found on maintenance and test equipment or portable media bound for CDAs)
deadline: Within 4 hours after discovery
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
owner: Station shift manager (decision), advised by the Site Cyber Security Program Manager

obligation: NRC cyber notification: attack initiated by personnel with access
trigger: Discovery of a suspected or actual cyberattack initiated by personnel with physical or electronic access to digital systems and networks within the scope of 73.54 (for example, an outage contractor with unescorted access)
deadline: Within 4 hours after discovery
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS; also inform the access authorization program
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
owner: Station shift manager (decision), advised by the Site Cyber Security Program Manager

obligation: NRC cyber notification: after notifying another agency
trigger: Notification to a local, State, or other Federal agency (for example, the FBI or CISA) of an event related to the licensee's cyber security program for systems within the scope of 73.54 that does not otherwise require a 73.77(a) notification
deadline: Within 4 hours after the notification to the other agency
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. **The SOC must notify every affected station before any external report (POL-03 4.2), because the SOC's call starts this clock**
clock_starts: Time of the notification to the other agency
owner: Station shift manager (decision), advised by the Site Cyber Security Program Manager

obligation: NRC cyber notification: intelligence gathering or pre-operational planning
trigger: Receipt or collection of information on observed behavior, activities, or statements that may indicate intelligence gathering or pre-operational planning related to a cyberattack against systems within the scope of 73.54 (for example, the attacker searched business file shares for CDA inventories or network diagrams)
deadline: Within 8 hours after receipt or collection of the information
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Receipt or collection of the information
owner: Station shift manager (decision), advised by the Site Cyber Security Program Manager

obligation: Corrective action program entry: cyber program weaknesses
trigger: Vulnerabilities, weaknesses, failures, and deficiencies in the 73.54 cyber security program, whoever discovers them
deadline: Within 24 hours of discovery
notify: Station corrective action program (record, not a notification)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Corrective action program entry: notifications made
trigger: Any notification made under 73.77(a)
deadline: Within 24 hours
notify: Station corrective action program
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Written security follow-up report
trigger: A telephonic notification made under 73.77(a)(1), (a)(2)(i), or (a)(2)(ii). Not required after (a)(2)(iii) or (a)(3) notifications, or after a retraction made before the report was submitted
deadline: Within 60 days of the telephonic notification
notify: NRC on NRC Form 366 under 73.4, with a copy to the Director, Office of Nuclear Security and Incident Response; SGI or classified content handled under 73.21-73.22 or Part 95
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
owner: Site Vice President (signs); station Licensing prepares

obligation: Retraction of a cyber notification
trigger: A previous 73.77 report is determined not to meet the reporting threshold
deadline: By telephone when the determination is made (no fixed clock); include the report retracted and the basis
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Determination that the threshold was not met
owner: Station shift manager (decision), advised by the Site Cyber Security Program Manager

obligation: Safeguards Information in a notification
trigger: A notification that would contain SGI or classified information
deadline: Same clock as the notification
notify: Secure communications: call the commercial number and request transfer to a secure telephone; if secure communications are unavailable, give the required information without SGI and say so; SGI may be sent without secure systems under the 73.22(f)(3) emergency exception
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
owner: Station shift manager (decision), advised by the Site Cyber Security Program Manager

obligation: Emergency declaration and ERDS
trigger: The emergency plan classification criteria are met (for example, a cyber event that affects plant safety or security functions)
deadline: Immediately after notifying state and local agencies and not later than 1 hour after declaring the emergency class; ERDS activated not later than 1 hour after declaring an Alert or higher
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center; state and local agencies under the emergency plan
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if an emergency class is declared

obligation: Major loss of emergency assessment, offsite response, or offsite communications capability
trigger: The attack disables emergency communications or assessment capability (for example, offsite notification systems or the ERDS link)
deadline: Within 8 hours
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS. Indicate the 73.77 criteria if the event is also a cyber event (73.77(c)(7))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if those capabilities are lost
owner: Station shift manager (decision), advised by the Site Cyber Security Program Manager

obligation: News release or notification of other government agencies
trigger: Any event or situation related to the health and safety of the public or onsite personnel, or protection of the environment, for which a news release is planned or notification to other government agencies has been or will be made
deadline: Within 4 hours
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the event relates to public or onsite health and safety or the environment. A business network cyber event alone is assessed under 73.77(a)(2)(iii) and 73.1200(e)(3) instead
clock_starts: Plan for the release or the agency notification

obligation: Physical security event: law enforcement response likely to draw media inquiries
trigger: A law enforcement response to the facility (for example, FBI agents arriving on site) that could reasonably be expected to result in public or media inquiries and does not otherwise require a 73.1200 or 50.72(b)(2)(xi) notification
deadline: Within 4 hours after discovery
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - licensee subject to 73.55
owner: Shift manager with the Director, Nuclear Security

obligation: Physical security event: security system failure without timely compensatory measures
trigger: A failure, degradation, or vulnerability in a security or safeguards system (for example, alarm station software affected by the attack) for which compensatory measures were not employed within the required timeframe
deadline: Within 8 hours after discovery
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if security systems are affected and compensatory measures were late
owner: Shift manager with the Director, Nuclear Security

obligation: CIP-008-6 R4 Reportable Cyber Security Incident notification
trigger: A Cyber Security Incident that compromised or disrupted a high impact BES Cyber System at the Generation Dispatch Center (or its EACMS), as determined under the R1 Part 1.2 process
deadline: Within 1 hour after the determination
notify: E-ISAC and CISA, unless prohibited by law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - only if the GDC is affected. Station CDAs are under 73.54, not CIP
owner: Director, NERC Compliance (CIP Senior Manager informed)

obligation: CIP-008-6 R4 attempt to compromise notification
trigger: A Cyber Security Incident determined to be an attempt to compromise a high impact BES Cyber System at the GDC or its EACMS
deadline: By the end of the next calendar day after the determination
notify: E-ISAC and CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - only if the GDC is targeted

obligation: CIP-008-6 R4 updates
trigger: New or changed information about functional impact, attack vector, or level of intrusion
deadline: Within 7 calendar days of determining the new or changed information
notify: E-ISAC and CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - after any R4 report
clock_starts: Determination of new or changed information

obligation: Form DOE-417 (electric emergency incident and disturbance report)
trigger: Criteria 1 to 27 (for example, a cyber event that causes interruptions of electrical system operations)
deadline: Emergency Alert (criteria 1-9): within 1 hour; Normal Report (10-13): within 6 hours; Attempted Cyber Compromise (14): end of the next calendar day after the determination; System Report (15-27): later of 24 hours after recognition or end of the next business day; final report within 72 hours
notify: DOE CESER (DOE-417 online system)
applies_at_this_tier: Check: only if the company is a respondent under the form instructions. In this scenario the GDC is not affected; the GDC gives the host Balancing Authorities any information they need for their own reports
clock_starts: Time of the incident (or determination, for criterion 14)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
citation: Form 8-K Item 1.05(a); General Instruction B.1; Instruction 1 to Item 1.05
trigger: The disclosure committee determines that a cybersecurity incident is material. The determination must be made without unreasonable delay after discovery
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing through EDGAR, with Inline XBRL under Item 1.05(b))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant
clock_starts: Materiality determination (date and time recorded in the committee minute)

obligation: Form 8-K/A for information not available at filing
trigger: Information required by Item 1.05(a) was not determined or was unavailable at the time of the original filing (the original filing must say so)
deadline: Within 4 business days after the information is determined (without unreasonable delay) or becomes available
notify: SEC (amendment through EDGAR)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the original 8-K said information was not yet available
clock_starts: Determination or availability of the information

obligation: Attorney General delay of Item 1.05 disclosure
trigger: The U.S. Attorney General determines that disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Delay of up to 30 days, extendable by up to 30 more days and, in extraordinary circumstances (national security), a final 60 days
notify: Request goes through outside counsel to the Department of Justice; the company cannot grant itself a delay
applies_at_this_tier: Possible (a nuclear plant scenario may raise national security questions), never assumed
clock_starts: The date the Item 1.05 disclosure was otherwise due

obligation: Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K: risk management, strategy, and governance; describe whether risks from cybersecurity threats, including previous incidents, have materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect the company
deadline: With the Form 10-K
notify: SEC (Form 10-K)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: State data breach notification (each state where affected individuals reside)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example, "without unreasonable delay" or a fixed number of days); use outside counsel's state matrix and plan to the shortest clock
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractors and employees from many states (the outage contractor roster in this scenario covers 23 states)
clock_starts: Each state's own trigger (often discovery or determination of the breach)
owner: Chief Compliance Officer with outside counsel

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (for example, names with Social Security numbers in the outage contractor roster)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (15 more days only on written good cause to the Department under 501.171(3)(a)); law enforcement delay under 501.171(4)(b)
notify: Each affected Florida resident by mail or email (501.171(4)(d))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Florida worked example
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after the determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General), with the synopsis, count, services offered, a copy of the individual notice, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents are affected
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000 individuals are notified at once
clock_starts: Decision to notify more than 1,000 individuals

obligation: Florida no-harm determination
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years and provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely here (Social Security numbers were taken)

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (for example, the background screening vendor or payroll SaaS) has a breach
deadline: Vendor must notify the company as expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days after determining the breach or reason to believe it occurred
notify: The company (Chief Compliance Officer); the company then gives the notices it owes
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in vendor contracts (P03 G-107)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Report to law enforcement and CISA
trigger: Confirmed intrusion, ransomware, or extortion
deadline: As soon as practical. **Notify the affected stations first**: this report can start the 73.77(a)(2)(iii) 4-hour NRC clock
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - recommended
clock_starts: Time of the report (starts the 73.77(a)(2)(iii) clock)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (proposed)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief; 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. As proposed, the company would be covered (above the SBA size standard; owns commercial nuclear power reactors). Voluntary reporting to CISA is still recommended

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Outage contractor company notice
citation: Outage service contracts (contractors A and B and other suppliers)
trigger: Incident affecting the contractor's personnel data, accounts, or work at the station
deadline: Within 24 hours of confirmation (contract term)
notify: Contractor security and human resources contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: SL-1 and SL-2 client notice
citation: SL-1 monitoring and diagnostics agreements; SL-2 dosimetry processing agreements
trigger: Incident affecting client data or the services (for example, the M&D platform or the dosimetry portal)
deadline: Per contract (72 hours in the standard terms); clients decide their own regulatory notices
notify: Client security contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if SL-1 or SL-2 data or services are affected (not in this scenario)
owner: Vice President, Monitoring and Diagnostics Services; Director, Dosimetry Laboratory

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered under a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer (DoD contracts: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the company holds federal contracts or subcontracts with the clause (none in scope today)

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered under a federal contract
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer (DoD contracts: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the company holds federal contracts or subcontracts with the clause (none in scope today)
